one_liner: Vercel has a broad public REST API, self-serve access tokens, and an official MCP server.

auth.notes: OAuth supports integrations acting for users; personal access tokens support direct API access.

access.notes: The free Hobby plan can be the default team for API requests, and Vercel documents creating an API token from a personal account. Submitting a Marketplace integration requires review.

api.notes: The public reference covers deployment and project management, among other resources.

mcp.notes: Vercel documents its MCP server as available on all plans.

verdict.rationale: Vercel documents API requests against a default team that can be a free Hobby team, personal-account API-token creation, and a broad REST API. Submitting a Marketplace integration for review is distinct from making API requests.

evidence.quote: Vercel's IdP uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework, a widely adopted industry standard for securing and delegating access to resources on behalf of users.
Access Token : A bearer token your application uses to call the Vercel REST API for the permissions the user grants. This lasts for 1 hour
Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf.
Your default team will be used when you make a request through the API or CLI and don’t specify a specific team.
The first Hobby or Pro team you create will automatically be nominated as the default team.
The Hobby plan is free and includes a generous set of features on a per month basis:
Create a Vercel API access token from your personal account's Account Tokens page :
The Create Integration form must be completed in full before you can submit your integration for review.
All endpoints live under the URL https://api.vercel.com and follow the REST architecture.
You can deploy new versions of web applications, manage custom domains, retrieve information about deployments, and manage secrets and environment variables for projects.
Vercel MCP is Vercel's official MCP server.
Vercel MCP is available on all plans and your use is subject to Vercel's AI Product Terms .
Vercel is a platform for frontend frameworks and static sites, enabling developers to host websites and web services that deploy instantly, scale automatically, and require minimal configuration.

problems: Vercel does not state in one explicit sentence that Hobby users can create REST API tokens; the access finding rests on its linked account, default-team, and token instructions.
The initial Composio catalog search missed an accessible toolkit page.
The memo gives no quoted evidence for the deployment model.
name: Vercel

verification.note: OAuth 2.0 is documented for delegated access, and the resulting token calls the Vercel REST API for user-granted permissions. Separate Vercel access tokens authenticate API requests on the account holder’s behalf, which supports bearer_token; OAuth is the evidenced method for acting for users.

The Hobby plan is free, a Hobby team can be the default team for API requests, and token creation is documented from a personal account. The integration-submission review quote concerns Marketplace integrations, not obtaining API credentials.

The cited reference says endpoints live at api.vercel.com and follow REST, and it describes deploy, domain, deployment, secret, and environment-variable operations. That does not contradict breadth broad, and the quotes are from the stated public docs URL.
Vercel calls Vercel MCP its official MCP server and says it is available on all plans, with no quoted beta, pilot, or not-yet-launched limitation.
The quote is from a Composio toolkit page for Vercel.
Self-serve free credentials plus a documented, useful REST API support buildable_now with no main blocker. Marketplace review is separate from making API requests.
